title: Polynomial irreducibility and finite field extensions
terms: irreducible polynomial; minimal polynomial of an algebraic element; field extension; extension degree; tower law; finite field; algebraic element; algebraic closure; compositum of fields; Eisen- stein criterion; Gauss lemma.

exposition.text:
A nonconstant polynomial over a field is irreducible if it cannot be factored into two polynomi-
als of positive degree over that field. For degrees 2 and 3, this is equivalent to having no root
in the field; degree 4 can factor into two quadratics without a root. Gauss’s lemma says that a
primitive integer polynomial factors over Q exactly when it factors into positive-degree integer
polynomials; primitive means that the coefficients have gcd 1. Irreducibility after reduction
modulo a prime implies irreducibility over Q when the degree is preserved. Eisenstein’s crite-
rion applies when one prime divides all nonleading coefficients, not the leading coefficient, and
its square does not divide the constant coefficient.
A field extension K/F is a field K containing a specified copy of F ; its degree [K : F] is its
dimension as an F -vector space. An algebraic element α satisfies a nonzero polynomial over F,

question.text:
Which polynomial is irreducible over Q by Eisenstein’s criterion with prime 3?
5 3 5 3 5 5 3 5 3
(A) x + 6x + 9 (B) x + 6x + 1 (C) 3x + x + 3 (D) x + 6x + 3 (E) x + 3x + 6x

solution.text:
5 3
For x + 6x + 3, three divides every nonleading coefficient, does not divide the leading
coefficient, and nine does not divide the constant term three. Zero coefficients are divisible
by three. The other choices fail at least one required condition: their constant term is
divisible by nine, a nonleading coefficient is not divisible by three, or the leading coefficient
is divisible by three.

question.text:
2
The primitive polynomial p(x) = 2x + 3x + 1 reduces to the irreducible polynomial x + 1 over F .
2
Which statement is correct?
(A) p is irreducible over Q by reduction modulo two.
(B) p is reducible over Q; the reduction test does not apply because its degree drops.
(C) p is not primitive.
(D) p has no rational root.
(E) Every primitive polynomial of even leading coefficient is irreducible.

solution.text:
Over Z, p = (2x + 1)(x + 1), so it is reducible over Q. Modulo two, the first factor becomes
the constant one and the degree drops from two to one. The degree-preservation hypothesis
is essential in the reduction criterion. The coefficients have gcd one, so primitivity does
hold and is not the failed assumption.
